issues.issue: AGI and ASI appear before their full names or meanings.
issues.evidence: The chapter opening lists “AGI. ASI.” and later refers to both acronyms before expanding them in the breadth section.

issues.issue: The opening definition does not reliably separate AI from ordinary software.
issues.evidence: AI is defined as computer systems that “interpret information and produce a useful result,” which also describes many conventional programs. The definition supplies no dependable boundary for deciding what counts as AI.

issues.issue: Ordinary automation is presented as the representative rule-based AI mechanism.
issues.evidence: The transaction example contains one threshold-and-country trigger. It does not show a specialist knowledge base or reasoning across connected rules, so it teaches the reader to call a simple business rule AI.

issues.issue: Internal taxonomy language replaces the reader’s natural question.
issues.evidence: The transition asks “what job is this part of the system doing?” without establishing which system or part is meant. “Some labels describe the job” then exposes the producer’s organising framework instead of advancing a concrete explanation.

issues.issue: The move from AI to machine learning to job labels has no continuous causal or chronological spine.
issues.evidence: After defining AI, the chapter introduces two construction approaches and abruptly changes to recognition, ranking, recommendation and generation. It does not show what problem in the preceding explanation requires this new distinction.

issues.issue: A human video-shop clerk is used where an actual AI-system mechanism is required.
issues.evidence: The clerk classifies, estimates, ranks and recommends films, but the passage does not trace an AI system doing those operations. The reader must translate and debug a human analogy instead of seeing the claimed mechanism.

issues.issue: The history section arrives after the taxonomy and interrupts rather than builds the mental model.
issues.evidence: The chapter completes breadth claims and then inserts “AI did not begin with ChatGPT” before returning to product synthesis. The timeline does not cause the preceding organisation and makes the reader reorganise the chapter retrospectively.

issues.issue: Locally clear definitions do not add up to a reconstructable chapter route.
issues.evidence: The reader receives approaches, jobs, modalities, action properties, breadth claims and history in successive blocks, but the chapter does not provide one causal or chronological reason for that complete order. The final six-branch framework is supplied after the reader has already had to infer it.

registeredDefectsFoundUnaided: Ordinary automation was taught as rule-based AI.
Internal taxonomy language replaced the reader’s question.
The teaching order did not build.
A human action was presented as though it explained AI.

issues.issue: The promised chronological and causal spine is historically misleading.
issues.evidence: The chapter says “First came AI built from human knowledge,” calls machine learning “the next major approach,” then moves through predictive AI, deep learning, generative AI, multimodal AI, agentic AI and embodied AI. Neural-network, machine-learning, robotics and agent research overlapped rule-based work; embodied and agent ideas did not arise after generative and multimodal systems in this order. The later timeline admits overlap but cannot retroactively repair the main teaching route.
issues.repair: Stop presenting the entire label sequence as historical succession. Use history only for genuine developments: human-supplied knowledge versus learned patterns, greater practical capability from deep learning and the recent accessibility or popularity of generative, multimodal and agentic products. Introduce cross-cutting properties explicitly as questions about a current system, not as the next inventions.

issues.issue: Several major transitions lack a causal reason and therefore fail the required continuous-section test.
issues.evidence: Predictive AI does not create the need to explain deep learning; multimodal AI does not create the need for agentic AI; agentic AI does not historically lead to embodied AI. These are adjacent curriculum blocks rather than links in one discoverable argument.
issues.repair: Give each transition a reader-visible need. For example: after construction approaches, ask what results systems produce; after result types, ask what information they can connect; after inputs and outputs, ask whether the system only responds or can continue through actions; then separately ask whether those actions reach the physical world.

issues.issue: The synthesis is followed by the history that should have qualified the route before synthesis.
issues.evidence: “Put the labels together on one real product” appears before “A short timeline of the ideas.” The synthesis therefore appears to settle relationships before the chapter reveals that the methods and labels overlap historically.
issues.repair: Place the bounded history before final synthesis, or integrate only the history needed at each transition. Keep the product synthesis as the chapter’s earned click immediately before application.

issues.issue: Chapter 1 exceeds the governing orientation boundary and assesses mechanisms assigned to later chapters.
issues.evidence: The curriculum matrix assigns full teaching of expert systems and machine learning to Chapter 3, deep learning to Chapter 5, predictive mechanisms to Chapter 6, generative mechanisms to Chapter 7, multimodal and embodied mechanisms to Chapter 8 and agents to Chapter 10. R8 supplies mechanism-level explanations and then tests several labels as if Chapter 1 had taught them fully.
issues.repair: Keep Chapter 1 to plain orientation, the relationships among labels and their current/disputed/hypothetical evidence status. Route full mechanism claims and stronger assessment to their canonical later chapters.

issues.issue: The assessment does not provide the promised exact correction routes and does not adequately test the whole model.
issues.evidence: Recognise, Explain, Draw and Use provide answers, but no wrong answer routes the reader back to the exact repairing passage. Explain tests only the AI–machine-learning–deep-learning nesting; it does not test the full landscape. The five recognition cases reward label matching more than reconstruction of the chapter’s organising model.
issues.repair: Make the final transfer case require the reader to identify construction, result, modality, action, embodiment and breadth separately, including justified unknowns. For each misconception, point back to the exact section that repairs it.

issues.issue: The chapter does not reconnect to the whole-book mental model or hand off to Chapter 2.
issues.evidence: After Key Definitions, sources and three LAiDIES links, R8 simply ends. It never states what Chapter 1 added to the complete AI-system model or why the reader is now ready to follow an ordinary request through a product, model, software and hardware.
issues.repair: End with a compact reconstruction of what the labels can and cannot establish, followed by a plain Chapter 2 question about what happens after the reader presses Send.

issues.issue: The technical centre and ending do not sustain the locked LAiDIES teaching relationship.
issues.evidence: The Introduction has Ali’s cadence, conviction and direct relationship. Much of Chapter 1 becomes symmetrical textbook exposition with isolated jokes about kettles, filing cabinets, emotional winters, librarians and Swiss Army knives. The checks, definitions, sources and links end in generic textbook register rather than the smartest, enthusiastic Rewind Era best friend carrying the reader through the difficult centre.
issues.repair: Preserve the plain technical explanations but rewrite transitions, worked examples and the landing in Ali’s conversational cadence. Use fewer but more precise workplace or Rewind Era references that perform an explanatory job, and let one sustained narrator relationship connect the mechanism to the reader’s decisions.

issues.issue: The AI definition remains somewhat porous at its boundary with conventional computation.
issues.evidence: “Use information to work out a result for a task” improves on R7 and excludes simply stored answers, but many ordinary algorithms also compute results from information. The surrounding examples help, yet the definition alone is not a reliable classification test.
issues.repair: State that AI is a field with contested boundaries, then anchor this book’s practical use of the term in systems applying represented knowledge, search, optimisation or learned patterns to tasks such as recognition, prediction, generation and planning.

sectionChain.why: The Introduction establishes why the reader needs practical, news and civic AI literacy; Chapter 1 begins with the confusing public labels she must learn to interrogate.
Before separating public labels, the reader needs the largest shared term they are describing.
A human-knowledge approach can demonstrate that AI is broader than machine learning, but “First came” falsely presents it as the field’s single historical starting approach.

The maintenance burden and brittleness of supplied rules create a useful reason to introduce learning patterns from examples, although calling it the next historical approach overstates a clean succession.
After learning how working patterns can come from examples, the reader can see one major use of those patterns: estimating something about a new case.

Deep learning is a construction method inside machine learning, not a result category caused by predictive AI. The chapter gives no reason the reader must leave result types and return to construction at this point.
Deep learning supports many current generative systems, so it can prepare the reader to distinguish internal prediction from the visible creation of new content.
A generated output naturally raises the separate question of which forms of information a system can connect, but multimodality is not a chronological successor to generation.

Working across information forms does not create or explain multi-step goal pursuit. The transition changes from an information property to a system-control property without making that need explicit.
The agentic example acts in software, which creates a useful contrast with systems whose sensing or actions reach physical equipment.
After several capability properties, the chapter explicitly changes to the separate question of how broad a system’s uses are.
Current broad usefulness creates the exact misconception the disputed AGI proposal must distinguish.
Once disputed general intelligence is bounded, the reader can distinguish the still larger hypothetical claim of capabilities beyond the best human abilities.
After current, disputed and hypothetical breadth claims are separated, applying all relevant labels to one real product can expose overlap and prevent an AGI inference.

The timeline supplies qualifications needed to prevent the earlier route from looking like a linear historical ladder. Placing it after synthesis makes the reader revise an organisation the chapter has just presented as settled.

sectionChain.to: Recognise, Explain, Draw and Use checks
sectionChain.why: Once relationships and historical overlap are available, the reader can attempt reconstruction and application.
A compact lookup section can support later retrieval after the reader has attempted explanation and application.
The chapter ends with destinations but no recap of the mental model, no statement of what remains unresolved and no causal handoff to Chapter 2.

explainBack.response: Ordinary automation follows a predetermined instruction, such as routing every expense above a fixed amount to a manager. A rule-based expert system contains a body of specialist knowledge and applies several connected reasoning rules to the facts of a new case; it can combine findings and exclusions to reach a bounded conclusion. Artificial intelligence is the wider field. Machine learning is one approach inside AI that develops useful patterns from examples rather than depending only on rules written case by case. Deep learning is one kind of machine learning that uses neural networks with many connected layers to learn complicated representations. Predictive AI estimates something about a case, such as its category, value, order or likely outcome. Generative AI constructs new content for a request, although it may use repeated predictions internally while doing so. Multimodal means the system can connect more than one form of information, such as speech and an image; it is not a claim about breadth or intelligence. Agentic means the complete system can hold a goal, take steps, use permitted tools, inspect results, adjust and stop or ask for help. Embodied means AI is connected to physical sensors or machinery so it can sense or act in the physical world. Specialised AI has a bounded area of work. General-purpose AI supports many kinds of work, but broad usefulness does not prove robust intelligence in unfamiliar situations. Artificial general intelligence is a disputed proposed category for broadly adaptable intelligence across unfamiliar intellectual work; there is no universally accepted definition or test. Artificial superintelligence is hypothetical intelligence greatly beyond the strongest human capabilities across most or all important intellectual areas.

unseenTransfer.response: The workplace assistant is an AI system if it interprets the photographed fault and spoken description rather than merely storing or forwarding them. It is multimodal because it connects image and audio information. Recognising the equipment or classifying the visible fault may be a predictive or recognition job, but that label is justified only if the system actually estimates those properties rather than receiving them from another source. Drafting the report is generative because it creates new text. Checking the approved maintenance system and deciding to stop before submission can make the complete system agentic if it holds the repair-report goal, uses the approved tool, examines the returned information and applies a stopping or approval condition. It is specialised because the described product has a bounded maintenance task. It is not embodied merely because it reads a photograph or uses software; no physical sensor under its control, machine body or physical action is described. It is not justified to call it general-purpose, artificial general intelligence or artificial superintelligence. Unknown facts include: whether it was built with machine learning; whether it uses deep learning; whether the photograph and speech are interpreted by one multimodal model or separate components; how accurately it identifies faults; whether it retrieved the correct equipment record; what permissions it has in the maintenance system; whether stopping was a designed human-approval checkpoint or a failure; who verifies the drafted report; whether it can ever submit an order; what data it stores; and what happens when the image, speech and maintenance record conflict.

voice.beginning: PASS: the preserved Introduction has Ali’s conviction, direct address, comic timing, Rewind Era references and clear best-friend relationship. The Chapter 1 PowerPoint opening continues that relationship effectively.
voice.middle: FAIL: the technical centre is predominantly polished textbook prose arranged in highly regular sections. Individual jokes are competent, but they are usually detachable punch lines rather than a sustained LAiDIES narrator helping the reader discover the mechanism. Rewind Era teaching references largely disappear.
voice.ending: FAIL: the synthesis, exercises, definitions, sources and destination list become generic textbook apparatus. “An arrow in PowerPoint is not a time machine” is a strong isolated line, but the chapter does not finish with Ali’s conversational energy, a useful whole-book reconnection or an earned Rewind Era landing.

limitations: This was a read-only semantic review; no repository files were changed.
The verdict covers the exact R7 and R8 Markdown artifacts and the named internal authorities.
No rendered book interface was supplied, so layout, interaction behaviour and visual accessibility were not reviewed.
No external source or live product claim was independently re-verified on the web; factual currency was judged against the supplied research packet and its recorded 10 August 2026 check date.
No maker self-review or release receipt was used to form the artifact-first R7 or R8 verdict.
